overview.body:
**Mamaqucha** ​(*mamaqucha*) ‌— ‌Sea, Fishermen ​· ​Mother ​sea ​— ​belongs to ‌the ​Incan ​tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under ‌the ​domain ​"Sea, Fishermen". ​The ​name ​means ‌"Mother ​sea".

**Mamaqucha** ‌is ​sea, ‌fishermen. ​The ‌name means ​"Mother ‌sea" ​and ​belongs ‌to ‌the incan ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name as ​**Mamaqucha** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/mamaqucha/). ​The ​restoration ​needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ‌or ​diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form ​would ‌lose, ‌which ‌places ‌the name ​in ‌Tier ​2. ​The ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*mamaqucha* ​survives ​as ‌a modern ​convenience ​imposed ​by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the fallback, ‌is ​the ​form ​the ​project defends ‌as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation survives ‌for ​this name; ​**Mamaqucha** ​is a ​scholarly transliteration ​of ‌the reconstructed ​spoken form. ​Etymologically ‌the name ​means "Mother ‌sea".

​The ASCII ‌form ​*mamaqucha* survives ​only because ​the ​early domain-name ​system could ‌not ​carry diacritics; ‌it is ​a ‌technological compromise, ​not ‌an ancient ​spelling. The ‌Unicode ​restoration **Mamaqucha** ​recovers the ‌full ‌diacritic detail ‌of the ​scholarly ​transliteration directly ‌in ​the address ​bar. The ‌restoration ​needs no ​distinctive letters ‌or ​diacritics its ‌ASCII form ​would ​lose, which ​places ​the name ‌in Tier ‌2.

​The letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

​- ​**m** → ‌**M** — ‌Same, ‌capitalized
- ‌**a** ​→ **a** ‌— Same
​- ​**m** → ​**m** — ‌Same
​- **a** ​→ **a** ​— ‌Same
- ​**q** ​→ **q** ​— Same
‌- ​**u** → ‌**u** — ​Same
‌- **c** ​→ **c** ‌— ‌Same
- ​**h** ​→ **h** ​— Same
​- ‌**a** → ‌**a** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/mamaqucha/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**mamaqucha** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Mamaqucha.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"mamaqucha" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Mamaqucha".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"mamaqucha" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Mamaqucha" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Mamaqucha was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Mamaqucha ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Mamaqucha ‌place ​sea, fishermen ​at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living ​mythological world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Mamaqucha ‌appears ​in incan ‌tradition ​as ​sea, fishermen. ​The ​name's ​meaning, "Mother ‌sea", ​shapes the ‌narratives ​told ‌about this ​figure.

‌### ​Worship and ‌Memory ​(Cult)

​Devotees and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ‌Mamaqucha ​in ​ritual, text, ‌and ​iconography, ​ensuring the ‌name ​survived ​into the ‌modern ​scholarly record.

‌The ​myths ​of Mamaqucha ​survive ​in ‌fragments, summaries, ‌and ​later ‌retellings. Each ​version ​reflects the ‌interests ‌of ‌its tellers ‌— ​poets, ‌priests, philosophers, ​and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does not ​privilege ​a ‌single version; ​it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. The ​restoration ‌Mamaqucha ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Mamaqucha ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Incan ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Mamaqucha, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​sea ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Mamaqucha ‌is to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of ​sea, Fishermen ‌in ​the ​mind ‌and ​to ask ‌what ​of ‌it ​endures. ​The name ​means ​"Mother ​sea" ‌— ​and a ‌name ​that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning so ​openly ‌invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere recollection. ‌The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​sea, ‌Fishermen ​· ​Mother ‌sea.

Sit ​with ‌the ​restored ​form ​— Mamaqucha ​— ‌and ‌the ​diacritics ‌themselves become ​the ​practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ‌a small ​act ‌of ​attention, ​a ​refusal to ‌let ​the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form *mamaqucha* ​stand ​in ​for ‌the ​whole. What ‌the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this name, ‌the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader to ‌preserve ‌in ​turn.
